notes: SUMMARY: Lodestar builds conversational layers for hospital EHR interfaces. They need predictable latency (patient-facing) and strict residency (EU + US PHI).
Workload profile (customer): mixed — 60% short chat requests (10-40 tokens output), 30% summarization (avg 1200 tokens), 10% embeddings/rerank jobs batched overnight.

Baseline metrics from workshop: steady-state QPS 18 for short prompts, peak QPS spikes to 140 during morning rounds. Avg prompt length 60 tokens in production. Token/sec baseline (observed) ~ 1,150 tokens/sec aggregated across 6 service nodes during peak sample window.

Redwood sizing recommendation: start Dedicated pool = 4 x A10G equiv GPUs for steady-state with 2x burst headroom (policy-based), quantified as ~32 vbatch capacity for chat-critical paths. Proposed two-week POC using 4x GPUs + prefix cache config.

Latency SLO ask: 95th percentile <120ms for short chat (<=40 tokens) and <600ms for long summarization flows (>=1k tokens). They're willing to accept token-level tailing for large generation but need guardrails for patient UX.
Cost sensitivity: procurement flags upper ARR cap — prefer monthly committed capacity with predictable unit cost; want fallback to lower-cost quantized model for night batch rerank jobs.
Security notes: strict KMS integration (bring-your-own-key), audit-log retention 7 years, SAML SSO + SCIM, formal penetration test report required before production enablement.
Quotes from workshop: 'We need guarantees — not just averages. Morning spike killed the prototype in prod last month.' — A. Ramirez, CTO
Operational asks: token-level cost breakdown in Console, per-route throttling by customer tier, automatic fallback to smaller model family when capacity constrained.
